gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Peak Design Travel Tripod's built-in ball head can be swapped for any standard third-party head with Peak Design's own $29.95 Universal Head Adapter (you change it with the included hex wrench, and it works with or without the center column), or that its clamp takes ordinary Arca-type plates.
standout_why: I compared against three rival pages. findingtheuniverse.com, which ChatGPT cited in the second chat, says the Peak Design head 'is integrated… so you can't swap it for a different head later' and lists its plate as 'Proprietary'. Peak Design's own adapter page contradicts the first claim, and Dan Carr's photos of RRS and Acratech heads on the tripod's own clamp contradict the second. digitalnomads.world, cited in the first chat, says only that the head is integrated, does not say whether it comes off, and tells Arca users to 'check compatibility and adapters'. amateurphotographer.com, cited in both chats, returned HTTP 403, so I could not compare against it. None of the pages I could read mention the Universal Head Adapter.
decides: This keeps the Peak Design Travel Tripod in play for shoppers who were told it locks them in. Anyone who wants a fluid video head, a panoramic head or a ball head they already own can use the Peak Design legs for $29.95 more, and their existing Arca plates should work in the stock clamp. It does not change the order for a shopper who will only use the stock head. For the Ulanzi Zero Y, the head that comes on it is the one you keep: digitalnomads says it is 'designed as part of the tripod rather than a standard user-detachable head' and gives a 3 kg ball-head payload. I could not open Ulanzi's own page to confirm whether a center-column accessory gets around this.

findings.label: Replacing the stock head with a third-party head
findings.value: Universal Head Adapter, $29.95: 'Use Travel Tripod's ultra-compact legs with any standard 3rd party tripod head.' 'Simply replace the Compact Ball Head with the Universal Head Adapter (using included hex wrench).'
findings.source_title: Travel Tripod // Universal Head Adapter – Peak Design
findings.note: Maker's US page. It also says: 'Works with both carbon and aluminum Peak Design Travel Tripods. Works with or without the Travel Tripod center column.' The third-party head is sold separately. The page has an add-to-cart button but gives no stock count.

findings.label: Third-party heads mounted through the stock clamp with Arca plates
findings.value: An RRS BH-55 and an Acratech GXP, each mounted with an Arca-Swiss plate on the head's base
findings.source_title: Best Accessories for the Peak Design Travel Tripod – Shutter Muse (Dan Carr)
findings.note: Dan Carr: 'the best solution is to use an Arca-Swiss compatible plate on your ball head… attach the head to the tripod using the tripod's existing quick release clamp.' He photographed both heads mounted this way. This means the clamp takes Arca plates, which contradicts findingtheuniverse's 'Proprietary'. The page shows two dates: 2020-04-07 and 2025-12-05.

findings.product: Peak Design Standard Plate v3 (included with Travel Tripod)
findings.label: Plate compatibility
findings.value: 'Works with most ARCA-type tripods (including ours)'; '50% lower profile design'; sold separately for $19.95
findings.note: Maker's US page. It says the plate 'comes with Capture, Travel Tripod, and Clutch camera strap'. The page gives no thickness in mm.

findings.label: US store price
findings.note: This is the only price the page text shows, and it does not name the variant. It matches the aluminum price ChatGPT showed. I could not read a carbon price because the specs and variant tab did not render.

findings.label: Low-mode height
findings.note: Taken from the image alt text on the maker's page: 'Aluminum tripod in low mode which is 14.2cm tall.'

unsourced: Peak Design's own spec table for load capacity, weight and packed length, and its wording on plate and clamp compatibility. The specs tab did not render through the page fetcher, and storecheck.py returned HTTP 404 for both the tripod and the adapter.

Peak Design's own statement that the Travel Tripod clamp accepts 'all PD plates and most 3rd party Arca-type plates'. Search snippets quote it from retailer pages; I did not open a Peak Design page that says it.

Ulanzi Zero Y: the maker's own wording on head detachability, the F38 1/4 center-column workaround, ball-head payload, and US price. ulanzi.com returned HTTP 429 twice, as did storecheck. Adorama returned 403, and I could not extract text from the Clifton Cameras spec PDF.
Manfrotto Befree Advanced AS: removable 494 head, Arca plate and load rating from Manfrotto's US page. The URL I tried returned 404.
SIRUI Traveler 5C: load rating from SIRUI's own page. Retailer snippets disagree (4 kg vs 6 kg), and I did not open the maker's page.
Amateur Photographer best-tripod guide (cited by ChatGPT): returned HTTP 403, so I could not check whether it mentions the Universal Head Adapter.
